long_biography.plain_text:
Civil engineer Şarık Tara pursued difficult jobs that required unfamiliar techniques. At Gölcük, his team built a ship-launching slipway by casting concrete blocks on land and placing them on piles in the sea. Inside ENKA, he worked with former university classmates and encouraged open discussion rather than competition for authority.

Beyond construction, Tara worked to improve relations between Turkey and Greece. He helped bring their prime ministers together at Davos in 1988 and subsequently chaired the Turkish-Greek Business Council. His efforts continued through exchanges between the two business communities, giving the political dialogue a sustained commercial counterpart.
